_transcription: PAGE MAP - 12 rendered pages (idx 0..11 = printed folios 1..12), every index accounted for at FULL SIZE, not from the contact sheet. idx 0 = bilingual cover (Series AABB4/3, SET-2, Q.P. Code 56/3/2, 'CHEMISTRY (Theory)', Time allowed 2 hours, Maximum Marks 35, '12 printed pages'). ENGLISH = the EVEN indices 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (folios 3, 5, 7, 9, 11). HINDI = the ODD indices 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 (folios 2, 4, 6, 8, 10). idx 11 (folio 12) is BLANK - only a rule, an asterisk and the footer (56/3/2, 222 B, 12, QR). The alternating hypothesis held exactly: NO parity inversion, NO English-only final page. OVERFLOW CHECK: I stacked the top 30% of all five odd indices and read them together - idx 1 (Hindi General Instructions), idx 3 (Hindi Q2, Q3, then 'khand - kha' Q4, Q5), idx 5 (Hindi Q6 with its 'athava'), idx 7 (Hindi Q9), idx 9 ('khand - ga', Hindi Q12) - EVERY one opens in Hindi and carries NO English overflow anywhere. Each English page ends on a complete question, which is why nothing spills. QUESTION MAP: idx 2 = General Instructions + SECTION-A Q1; idx 4 = Q2, Q3 + SECTION-B Q4, Q5(+OR); idx 6 = Q6(+OR), Q7, Q8(+OR); idx 8 = Q9, Q10, Q11(+OR); idx 10 = SECTION-C Q12 passage + (a)-(d) and the (d) OR. STRUCTURE: the paper's own printed General Instructions agree with the term2_sci table exactly - 12 questions, three Sections, A = Q.1 to 3 at 2 marks, B = Q.4 to 11 at 3 marks, C = Q.12 case based at 5 marks (6+24+5 = 35), and there are NO MCQs anywhere on the paper or in the marking scheme. Two points where the paper disagrees with what I was told: it prints only SIX instructions (i)-(vi) and the sixth is 'Use of log tables and calculators is NOT allowed', so there is NO internal-choice line at all; and Q12 has FOUR sub-parts (a)-(d) at 1+1+1+2, not five - the fifth Section-C row is the OR alternative to (d). INTERNAL CHOICE: with no printed count, the roster was established by walking the marking scheme question by question and confirming each against a printed 'OR' on the English page and 'athava' on the Hindi one. It prints a bare OR for Q5, Q6, Q8, Q11 and Q12(d), and for NO other question - FIVE alternatives, all transcribed. Q10's (a)(b)(c) are compulsory parts, not a choice. Following the PAPER. No 0{\cdot} anywhere. CBSE-VOIDED: NONE. I swept all six marking-scheme pages (p00-p01 general instructions, p02-p05 the answer table, which ends '* * *') for 'full mark to be awarded', 'award full mark if attempted', 'printing error', 'error in question', 'no option is correct' and 'data given' - no such note exists. MARKING-SCHEME IDENTITY: confirmed two ways - its header reads '[ Paper Code: 56/3/2]' and its footer reads 'XII_39_043_56/3/2_Chemistry' on all six pages, and its worked answers match this paper's questions one for one (Q2 -> propanamide, Q6(b)(iii) -> cyclohexane, Q10(b) -> dibromidobis(ethane-1,2-diamine)cobalt(III) ion). questions._figure: ILLUSTRATIVE - parts (i) and (iii) are DRAWN rather than written. (i) draws the three carbonyls with explicit vertical C=O bonds and a vertical tert-butyl branch on the third; (iii) draws four benzene rings - inner alternating double bonds clearly present at 3x zoom, so genuinely aromatic, unlike the plain hexagon in Q6(b)(iii) - bearing COOH plus, respectively, NO2 at C-2 and C-4, NO2 at C-4, OCH3 at C-4, and nothing. Given that \(\mathrm{E^\circ}\)cell = 1.05V, IF = 96,500 \(\mathrm{Cmol^{-1}}\).

\(\mathrm{Fe(s)\,|\,Fe^{2+}\,(0.001\ M)\,||\,H^{+}\,(0.01M)\,|\,H_2(g)\,(1\ bar)\,|\,Pt(s)}\)

questions.subtopic: Temperature Dependence of the Rate of a Reaction
questions.context:
The rate of reaction is concerned with decrease in concentration of reactants or increase in the concentration of products per unit time. It can be expressed as instantaneous rate at a particular instant of time and average rate over a large interval of time. A number of factors such as temperature, concentration of reactants, catalyst affect the rate of reaction. Mathematical representation of rate of a reaction is given by rate law :
\(\mathrm{Rate = k[A]^{x}\,[B]^{y}}\)
x and y indicate how sensitive the rate is to the change in concentration of A and B. Sum of x + y gives the overall order of a reaction.
When a sequence of elementary reactions gives us the products, the reactions are called complex reactions. Molecularity and order of an elementary reaction are same. Zero order reactions are relatively uncommon but they occur under special conditions. All natural and artificial radioactive decay of unstable nuclei take place by first order kinetics.
questions.stem: What is the effect of temperature on the rate constant of a reaction ?
